name: Ricketts Glen State Park
summary: Glacial plateau camping in Benton, PA. Ground-truth guidance on the steep PA-487 Red Rock Mountain climb, non-electric main loops, pull-through electric loop specs, and dump station toad staging.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40 ft (strictly enforced; smaller loops capped at 30 ft)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate (unhook at main contact station / dump station lot)
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense mountain canopy; watch low-hanging oak/hemlock branches on loop curves
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Small Electric Loop (featuring longer pull-through pads)

approach.title: Mountain Grade & Route Clearance Warning
approach.text: Entering directly off PA State Route 487 requires tackling Red Rock Mountain—a severe 9% to 10% mountain grade coming from the south. Transmissions and brakes will be heavily tested. Heavy gas coaches and diesel pushers should gear down early and monitor engine temps on the climb.

recommendedGear.title: Recommended Rig Routing Gear
recommendedGear.reason: Ensures you are aware of steep mountain grades like PA-487 and calculates safe engine braking routes based on your total rig weight.

toadStrategy: Do not drag a towed vehicle directly into the dense inner non-electric loop. Drop your toad at the main park contact station or the nearby dump station staging area before proceeding to your site.

content.overview: Perched on the Allegheny Plateau, Ricketts Glen offers dense mountain woods and lake access. However, site types and hookups are split distinctly between loops, requiring careful site selection depending on your rig class.

recommendedGear.title: Recommended Campsite Leveling Gear
recommendedGear.reason: Mountain state park gravel pads frequently feature front-to-back slope. Curved levelers make dialing in level on uneven glacial soil quick and precise.

content.loopC: The smaller electric loop features generous pull-through sites designed for larger units, providing much easier backing angles and clearance from mature trees.
content.loopsAB: The larger main loop consists predominantly of non-electric, rustic sites tucked deep under a thick tree canopy. Turning radiuses on the inner curves are tight and best suited for smaller travel trailers, pop-ups, and Class C units.

name: Pequea Creek Campground
summary: Lancaster County camping along Pequea Creek in Pequea, PA. Critical big-rig routing warnings to bypass the low covered bridge, tight access road realities, and office turn-around intelligence.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40 ft (select sites accommodate larger configurations)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High (plenty of room to turn around past office with toad attached)
scorecard.treeClearance: Tight approach lanes; watch for low hanging branches on access roads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Sites near the main office and wider hookup sections

approach.title: Critical Approach & Low Clearance Warning
approach.text: There is a historic low covered bridge near the standard park entrance that must be avoided by most large RVs and motorhomes. Standard GPS apps will route you straight into this height restriction. Instead, enter via Bridge Valley Rd to Fox Hollow Rd and utilize the jughandle to safely enter the campground.

recommendedGear.title: Recommended Rig Routing Gear
recommendedGear.reason: Prevents low-bridge routing mistakes in Lancaster County by programming your exact rig height, length, and weight before calculating local approach roads.

toadStrategy: The main office is located past a large section of campsites, but there is ample room to maneuver and turn around even with a toad vehicle attached.

content.overview: Pequea Creek Campground offers a scenic Lancaster County retreat right along the water. However, navigating your motorhome or towing a vehicle here requires strict attention to your approach route to avoid infrastructure hazards.
content.loopC: The access road in is tight and bumpy, but it does allow adequate physical width for large RVs as long as you take your time and watch your tail swing.
content.loopsAB: Creekfront and hillside back-in sites vary in width and depth; take care when positioning slides around mature trees.

name: French Creek State Park
summary: Hopewell Big Woods camping in Elverson, PA. Verified breakdown of Loop C big-rig friendliness, inner-loop tree canopy clearance, and toad unhooking areas.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (strict site limitations apply)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate (unhooking recommended before inner loop entry)
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate overhead canopy on inner loops (watch roof AC/solar)

approach.title: Park Access & Road Conditions
approach.text: Main arterial state park roads are well-paved and wide enough for two large units to pass safely. Watch for tight interior loop turns once inside the park boundary.

toadStrategy: If you are towing a vehicle, do not drag your toad into the inner loops. Utilize the main registration/dump station parking area to drop your towed vehicle before proceeding back to your loop.

content.overview: French Creek’s campground is heavily wooded, offering a classic Pennsylvania state park ambiance with plenty of shade. While this canopy is wonderful during hot summer afternoons, it creates narrow lanes and tight turning radiuses. Inner loop pads can be uneven, making precise side-to-side leveling essential.

recommendedGear.title: Recommended Campsite Leveling Gear
recommendedGear.reason: State park sites often have sloping gravel and dirt pads. Curved levelers make independent, fine-tuned height adjustments fast and effortless without stacking blocks.

content.loopC: If you are driving a longer Class C or pulling a car behind you, Loop C is your safest bet. Loop C features wider pad openings and more generous backup angles.
content.loopsAB: Loops A and B skew toward smaller travel trailers, pop-ups, and camper vans. The turnarounds at the loops' edges are tighter.

name: The Great Divide Campground
summary: Sussex County camping in Newton, NJ. Full specs on pull-through vs wooded sites, steep hill grade warnings, G20–G25 big-rig recommendations, and toad staging lots.

scorecard.treeClearance: Clear on main arterial routes; moderate canopy on back loops

approach.title: Highway & Interior Access Grade
approach.text: Direct access off Route 519 is smooth and accessible for all rig classes, but climbing the main interior hill grade toward assigned upper loops requires momentum and proper toad staging.

toadStrategy: Disconnect at the main staging lot near the office before climbing the interior hill grade into assigned loops.

recommendedGear.title: Essential Towing & Staging Gear
recommendedGear.productName: Blue Ox Tow Bar & Heavy-Duty Drop Hitch
recommendedGear.reason: Disconnecting your toad on an incline under tension risks binding your tow bar. A high-quality setup makes unhooking seamless at the front office staging lot.

content.overview: Located in scenic Sussex County, The Great Divide combines open pull-through sections with wooded perimeter sites.
content.loopC: G-Section features full hookups and 50-amp service with long pad lengths suitable for heavy rigs.
content.loopsAB: Back wooded loops require navigating a brief steep grade.

name: Wading Pines Camping Resort
summary: Pine Barrens camping along the Wading River in Chatsworth, NJ. Ground-truth guidance on approach routes, overhead pitch pine clearance, 50-amp pull-through pads, and toad staging options.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (select oversized pull-throughs up to 60 ft)
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate overhead pine branches along interior sandy lanes

approach.title: Pine Barrens Route & Entrance Clearance
approach.text: Approaching via Route 563 to Godfrey Bridge Road is clear and flat. Watch for low-hanging pitch pine branches along the sandy entrance lane as you pull up to the gatehouse.

toadStrategy: Unhooking up front can be tight during peak weekend check-ins. Either unhook directly on your pull-through pad or bypass the gate to the rear corner overflow lot.

content.overview: Located deep in the New Jersey Pine Barrens along the Wading River.

recommendedGear.title: Essential Staging & Stabilization Gear
recommendedGear.productName: Camco Heavy-Duty RV Wheel Chocks & Leveling Blocks
recommendedGear.reason: Pine Barrens back-in sites feature soft sandy shoulders and subtle slopes. Having reliable chocks and interlocking blocks prevents shifting when parked on loose ground.
recommendedGear.loopC: 50-amp pull-through sites offer straight pull-in convenience.
recommendedGear.loopsAB: Inner wooded back-in loops feature soft sandy shoulders requiring leveling blocks.
